aspects.says: acquire(n) and tryAcquire(n) take all n permits together or none, including when interrupted, so a waiting job never holds part of what another needs.
basis: section:acquire(n) Takes All n Permits at Once or None

aspects.says: acquire() waits without bound, tryAcquire(timeout) waits a bounded time, tryAcquire() decides at once; checking availablePermits() before acquire() is a race.
basis: section:When the Permits Run Out, Choose: Wait, Wait a Bounded Time, or Refuse

aspects.says: Permits bound how many calls run at once, not how many start per second; a permit is reused as soon as it is released.
basis: section:A Semaphore Counts Permits: It Limits How Many Threads Are Inside, Not Which Ones

aspects.says: A Semaphore(N) lets up to N threads into the guarded code at once; with N above 1 it does not protect the state they share.
basis: section:A Semaphore Counts Permits: It Limits How Many Threads Are Inside, Not Which Ones
aspects.reason: lost updates under a multi-permit semaphore are a race whose outcome a deterministic test cannot force; the page shows a run

aspects.says: On a non-fair semaphore a waiting acquire(n) can be overtaken by smaller requests; a fair one queues them behind it.
basis: section:A Waiting acquire(n) Can Be Overtaken

aspects.says: Actions before a release() happen-before actions after a successful acquire in another thread.
basis: section:A Semaphore Keeps a Release Nobody Waited For, Which Makes It a Signal
aspects.reason: a memory-visibility guarantee that a deterministic test cannot tell apart from a lucky run; the page cites the javadoc

aspects.says: A semaphore that starts at -k needs k+1 releases before a single acquire succeeds.
basis: section:A Semaphore Keeps a Release Nobody Waited For, Which Makes It a Signal

aspects.says: A semaphore tracks no owner: any thread may release, and a thread that asks for a permit it already holds waits for itself.
basis: section:A Semaphore Has No Owner and Trusts Every Release: Release Exactly What You Acquired

aspects.says: A permit is released in a finally, and only on the path where the acquire succeeded; a missed release shrinks the limit and a release without an acquire raises it.
basis: section:A Semaphore Has No Owner and Trusts Every Release: Release Exactly What You Acquired
section:Spot the Problem: A finally That Gives Back a Permit the Thread Never Got

aspects.says: A release with nobody waiting is kept as a permit, so a semaphore can count signals from other threads, and leftover permits carry over to the next use.
basis: section:A Semaphore Keeps a Release Nobody Waited For, Which Makes It a Signal

aspects.says: A pool that trusts every release hands one resource to two callers after a double give-back.
basis: section:A Semaphore Has No Owner and Trusts Every Release: Release Exactly What You Acquired

aspects.says: The untimed tryAcquire() takes a free permit even when threads are queued on a fair semaphore; tryAcquire(0, SECONDS) respects the queue.
basis: section:When the Permits Run Out, Choose: Wait, Wait a Bounded Time, or Refuse
